The chlorides of the elements in the third period behave in different ways when added to water,
depending on their structure and bonding.
L and M are each a chloride of an element in Period 3. A student investigated L and M and their
results are given.
L is a white crystalline solid with a melting point of 987K. L dissolves in water to form an
approximately neutral solution. Addition of NaOH(aq) to an aqueous solution of L produces a
white precipitate.
M is a liquid with a boiling point of 331K. M is hydrolysed rapidly by cold water to form a
strongly acidic solution, a white solid and white fumes.
Identify L and M.
